1.why: Volumetric flow rate Q equals cross-sectional area A multiplied by velocity v.

wrong.b: Area is not added to velocity.
wrong.c: Velocity is not divided by area.
wrong.d: Time is not multiplied directly here.

2.why: If a river widens and deepens, its cross-sectional area A increases, raising discharge.

wrong.c: Water temperature does not directly set flow rate.

3.why: Clearing river channels and planting trees reduces peak flood velocity and erosion.

wrong.a: Building concrete walls without care can worsen downstream surges.

_quiz_pool.question: What does Q stand for in river physics?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Q is the volume of water passing per second.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the unit of flow velocity v?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Velocity is distance divided by time (m/s).

_quiz_pool.question: If cross-sectional area A is 12 m² and velocity v is 4 m/s, Q is…
During heavy rain, why do rivers overflow?
_quiz_pool.explanation: When water volume and speed surge, Q exceeds what the channel can hold.

_quiz_pool.question: What does A represent in Q = A × v?
_quiz_pool.explanation: A is the area of the river channel cut.

_quiz_pool.question: Which agency monitors weather and rain globally?
_quiz_pool.explanation: NASA Earth Observatory tracks Earth systems.

_quiz_pool.question: What happens to river flow when heavy rain falls upstream?
What is the unit for cross-sectional area A?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Area is measured in square meters.

_quiz_pool.question: Which organisation handles disaster response and flood data?
_quiz_pool.explanation: NASA monitors flood and rain events.

_quiz_pool.question: Why do natural river bends slow down water flow?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Curves and friction slow down water movement.

physics.title: Calculating water discharge
physics.body_1: To find out how much water flows through a river, physicists calculate volumetric flow rate, Q. It depends on the size of the river channel and how fast the water moves.
physics.body_2: Cross-sectional area A is width times depth. Velocity v is how fast the water travels forward.
physics.assumptions: We assume steady, uniform flow across the cross-section and ignore friction losses along the riverbed.
table.note: Larger area and higher velocity create flood discharge.
